Jordi Visser ("Geordie Visser"): YouTube thesis, Jul 12 – Oct 12 2026 (v2, full read)

Rebuilt Mon 12 Oct 2026 (Sydney) for Chris, from a full start-to-finish read of all 14 weekly videos. Per-video notes are in notes/. The first draft is kept as THESIS_v1_draft.md.

Channel: Jordi Visser, @JordiVisserLabs (~74.8K subscribers, one long video a week, usually Sunday ~23:30 Sydney). Ex-Morgan Stanley (S&P options/ETF/program trading), then Weiss Multi-Strategy and 22V Research. The videos are educational, with "not advice" disclaimers.

Rules of this document:
- Every quote is a verbatim YouTube auto-caption, machine-checked against the cached transcript and linked to the start of its caption segment. Captions misspell names: "Marll" = Marvell, "Eli Liy" = Eli Lilly, "Robin Hood" = Robinhood, "Worsh" = Warsh.
- "Inferred" = our reasoning from his framework, not his call.
- Desk data is from /workspace/minervini, session 2026-10-09 (Fri 9 Oct US close). RS is the desk's own calculation, not IBD's.

1. How he thinks (the framework to reuse)

  1. Long scarcity, short abundance. "you want to be short abundance. Anything built on code that can be replicated by a computer. And you want to be long scarcity." (2026-07-12 @ 11:04) Scarce: compute, memory, power, optics, Bitcoin. Abundant: models, software, code. "Intelligence can be copied powered can be copied. Powered compute cannot." (2026-07-26 @ 23:12)
  2. Agents are the demand side. This is the core causal claim: past bubbles had human demand, but now billions of agents consume tokens 24/7, so supply can't catch up. "Demand is still greater than supply." (2026-10-11 @ 7:21) "It is impossible to get enough compute for all of the billions of agents that are coming online that are just starting." (2026-08-16 @ 4:23)
  3. Own the receivers of capital, not the spenders. "I want to belong the receivers of the capital because the infrastructure demand is insatiable." (2026-08-16 @ 20:11) Hyperscalers and consumer-agent platforms fight over the same TAM, so "do not play the game of trying to figure out who's going to win the personal agent game." (2026-10-11 @ 21:09) — "You want to be long agent trades. Most of that is compute." (2026-10-11 @ 20:51)
  4. Step-up functions. He hunts for discontinuous earnings or guidance jumps (Micron after Opus 4.5, Rogers' investor day, Vera Rubin/800V DC), then maps the supply chain behind each one. "because it was a step up and I love stepups." (2026-10-04 @ 23:17)
  5. Sequencing the waves. Phase 1 was compute/brains plus power (Nvidia, Vistra, turbines). Phase 2 was memory (after Opus 4.5). Phase 3 is consumer agents, which bring more tokens, edge AI, and crypto rails as the "financial guardrails". Phase 4 is physical AI (humanoids, FSD). "I think it's time now to start talking about humanoids and FSD" (2026-10-11 @ 41:43)
  6. Time compression kills terminal value, so multiples compress even for winners: the "Nvidia mud trap". "That is called moving higher in mud. That's the Nvidia mud trap." (2026-08-23 @ 66:54) — "in the end, I believe all of them will go through multiple compression." (2026-09-27 @ 20:19) He's bearish on most public equities by 2030, but "not today".
  7. Long speed, short friction. "you want to be long speed and short friction" (2026-09-27 @ 42:23) The "bear market inside a bull market": rising rates "get rid of the weak" (rate-dependent old economy, legacy SaaS, banks, card networks) while the digital economy compounds. "There is a bubble in companies that would have been gone a long time ago around the globe if it wasn't for the fact that rates kept them in business." (2026-10-11 @ 8:51)
  8. Facts over stories, and the tape. His recession signal is S&P year-over-year turning negative: "If year-over-year S&P goes negative, I'll change my mind." (2026-09-27 @ 10:08) He treats bubble-call magazine covers (Dalio, "Will bonds blow up?") as contrarian signals.

What he watches (his dashboard), which maps onto Chris's toolkit:
- Breadth within his 100-name basket: % above the 20/50/200-day, and whether the 200-day is rising.
- 50-day rate of change of the basket (risk rises above ~20%).
- ATR% contracting, which he reads as "coiled".
- His trend stages: out-of-trend → resetting → coiled → ignition → trending: "80 plus% are above the 200 day moving average with their 200 day moving average pointed upward." (2026-09-13 @ 24:11) This is essentially a Stage-2 / VCP lens.
- Cross-asset ratios: staples/S&P and financials/utilities (defensive rotation = real warning), equal-weight vs cap-weight with MACD buy signals, IWM/QQQ, HYG/IEF and CCC vs HY spreads (credit), tech-momentum factor vol.
- Crypto: the BTC 200-day (and its slope) and DOGE as the "retail energy" gauge.
- Scarcity prices: GPU rental rates and DRAM contract prices.
- His exits: "until Bitcoin goes back under the 200 day moving average. That'll be the point that I bail out" (2026-08-23 @ 4:05) and, for crypto, "If we take out the lows, I'm out." (2026-09-06 @ 45:51)

2. How his view evolved (Jul → Oct)

Phase Videos Read Positioning
A. Speed crash, mid-cycle slowdown Jul 12 – Jul 26 Tech momentum had its worst unwind on record ("So this is by far by far the worst unwind we have seen in tech mo momentum momentum." (2026-07-19 @ 3:23)), but it's a structural bull market on token demand. Expect chop through the second half. Software is "toast". He'd sold all his Micron in May and rotated into silver, BTC and Lilly. He began re-buying MU in mid-July and added AAOI. MRVL was his biggest position.
B. Bottom call Aug 2 – Aug 16 The Situational Awareness fund blow-up = a cleansing event. "The speed crash has occurred, it's over. The bottom is in as far as I'm concerned on a probability basis." (2026-08-09 @ 14:27) Compute becomes an asset class. "Those who can't compete, compute". Bought "a decent amount" of NVDA plus MU and AAOI. Hedging = 50-day ROC plus breadth.
C. AI–crypto macro nexus Aug 23 – Sep 6 "Bitcoin does not get disrupted by AI. It is the purest AI trade." (2026-08-23 @ 1:41) BTC broke its 200-day. Fiat "double debasement". Infrastructure is "in the mud until the midterms". Largest positions: silver (SIL > SLV) and BTC, plus ETH and BitMine. NVDA grew to MRVL's size. "My AI stuff is smaller than crypto by a good amount, especially when you beta adjust it." (2026-09-06 @ 36:10)
D. AGI arrives; crypto breakout; Fed surprise Sep 13 – Sep 20 Astra = AGI. Crypto index at new highs ("This is the most important macro trade of everyone's existence." (2026-09-20 @ 2:22)). The Fed hiked 25bp, against his call. Meta's Muse launches consumer agents. "about 20% of my portfolio right now is in the AI trade. Back here it was about 80." (2026-09-20 @ 27:19) Still adding to crypto, not AI.
E. Bear market inside a bull; consumer agents = new compute wave; bank apocalypse Sep 27 – Oct 11 Muse is the week's #1 story. "I think the infrastructure trade has a catalyst." (2026-09-27 @ 33:28) The breadth washout is a bottoming signal. Banks, Visa and Mastercard are next to be disrupted. Lumentum sold out to 2029, Rogers stepped up. 2027 = compute + AI + crypto year. Still mostly crypto. Holds MRVL, NVDA and a smaller MU; personally holds NEAR. The infrastructure catalyst is back on his radar.

What changed and what didn't:
- Constant: structural bull, compute/memory scarcity, short abundance.
- Rotations: memory → silver/BTC/Lilly (May) → crypto-heavy (Aug–Sep) → back to "infrastructure has a catalyst" (late Sep/Oct), framed as a consumer-agent compute wave rather than enterprise capex.
- Gold: went from a debasement buy ("You should be buying gold, buying silver, buying Bitcoin." (2026-08-16 @ 41:49)) to "not the fastest horse" (Aug 30) to "broke down" (Oct 4).
- Hyperscalers: went from "don't be short" to "not bullish relative to infrastructure".

  • Themes v1 missed:

  • His own technical staging system and hedging tools (50-day ROC, breadth in the 100, ATR%).
  • Market-structure risk from tokenization: 24/7 trading hurts options and market-neutral funds.
  • Labor weakness becoming the next pressure on bonds.
  • AI biology / IP revaluation.
  • Physical AI as the next wave.
  • The privacy sub-theme.
  • The sector-breadth evidence that "rates only hurt the old economy".

  • notes/<date>_<id>.md: per-video full-coverage notes with verified quotes and links (sources in notes_src/, rendered by render_notes.py).

  • videos.json: the video list with transcript_status read_in_full, for the weekly diff.
  • desk.py: desk lookup (universe.json, stock/.json, wyckoff/.json, feeds/setups/latest.json).
